cards.text: This one's a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster. No battle, no palace, no enemies chasing him. David is just looking UP at the sky, and friend, he's about to tell us the sky has something to say.

cards.question: David looks up at the heavens. What does he say they declare?
True or false: David says the skies proclaim the work of God's hands.

cards.text: So how often does the sky make this big announcement? Friend, I've had ovens with less commitment than this.

cards.question: David says the sky pours forth speech and reveals knowledge. How often does it do that?

answers.text: Day after day and night after night
Only when the moon is full

cards.text: Now you'd think a message that big would come with a LOT of noise. Stadium noise. Fireworks noise.

cards.question: David says the sky speaks day and night. What does he say that speech sounds like?

answers.text: Without a sound to be heard
Like a trumpet blast at dawn

cards.text: No speech, no language, not ONE sound. Meanwhile I need a group chat and three reminder emails just to get one message across.

cards.question: Even without a sound, the sky's voice has gone out into all the ___.

cards.text: Then David turns to the brightest thing up there: the sun. God has set up a place for it to live in the heavens.

cards.question: In the heavens, God has pitched a ___ for the sun.

cards.text: Every morning the sun comes out of that tent, and David paints TWO pictures of it. I've got a soft spot for this first one, friend.

cards.question: True or false: David compares the rising sun to a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.
David's second picture of the rising sun is a champion. What is the champion doing?

cards.text: And it's OFF! The sun rises at one end of the heavens and runs its circuit clear to the other, and not once does it hit the snooze button.

cards.question: True or false: As the sun crosses the heavens, some things are left out of its warmth.

cards.text: Then, out of nowhere, David switches. One line he's on the sky, the next he's on the Law of the LORD, like a GPS that says "turn left" when you're already IN the intersection.

cards.question: David says the Law of the LORD is perfect. What does it do for the soul?
David says the testimony of the LORD is trustworthy. It makes the ___ wise.

cards.text: Next up: the precepts and the commandments of the LORD. Each one gets a description AND a gift.

cards.question: David says the precepts of the LORD are right, bringing ___ to the heart.

cards.text: The commandments are radiant, giving light to the eyes, and then the fear of the LORD and the judgments of the LORD get their turn. That's six in a row, every one a rave review, and I have never gotten ONE like that for a single cookie.

cards.question: David says the fear of the LORD is pure. How long does he say it endures?
True or false: David says the judgments of the LORD are true but only partly righteous.

cards.text: So how much is all of this worth? David goes for two big comparisons.

cards.question: David says everything he's been praising is more precious than ___ and sweeter than ___.

cards.text: Sweeter than honey from the comb, friend, and I bake for a LIVING, so that is a HIGH bar. Then David starts talking straight to God and calls himself "Your servant."

cards.question: David says God's servant is warned by these things. What does he say is in keeping them?

cards.text: Then David asks, "Who can discern his own errors?" Not me: I once frosted a whole tray of cookies before tasting one and finding out I forgot the SUGAR.

cards.question: David knows he can't spot all his own errors. What does he ask God to do?

answers.text: Show him who his enemies are
Give him more time to fix them

cards.text: Hidden faults are one kind of sin. But David has another kind on his mind too.

cards.question: True or false: David only prays about his hidden faults and never mentions willful sins.
True or false: David says that when God keeps him from willful sins, he will be blameless and cleansed of great transgression.

cards.text: And David closes the whole psalm with a prayer about two things: the words of his mouth and the meditation of his heart.

cards.question: David prays that the words of his mouth and the meditation of his heart will be ___ in God's sight.
In the very last line of the psalm, what two names does David call the LORD?

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from Psalm 19:2. It only asks how often the sky speaks and adds a joke. Its joke ('ovens with less commitment than this') also hints that the answer to card 5 is 'all the time,' which rules out the two 'only on…' wrong answers.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The 'you'd think… a LOT of noise' setup signals a twist, so the baker can tell card 7's answer is the quiet one. That rules out 'rolling thunder' and 'trumpet blast.' The card also tells nothing from Psalm 19:3 even though it cites it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Without a sound to be heard' doesn't fit the question 'what does he say that speech sounds like,' and it isn't the same kind of answer as the two 'Like…' wrong answers. It stands out as the odd one.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: Card 7 already covered verse 3. This card restates 'no speech, no language, not ONE sound' and adds a joke, so it doesn't move the passage forward. It works as a recap.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Saying each item gets 'a gift' rules out card 5's wrong answers 'grief' and 'shame,' because neither one is a gift.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Every one a rave review' gives away card 8. Once the baker reads that, they know the judgments aren't 'only partly righteous.' The card also packs in three beats: the commandments, the fear and judgments, and the six-in-a-row joke.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card carries more than two beats. It covers the commandments with their gift, then the fear of the LORD and the judgments, then the tally-and-cookie joke.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Saying 'David has another kind on his mind too' gives away card 16. The baker already knows David doesn't 'only' pray about hidden faults. The card also calls the hidden faults 'one kind of sin,' but the text calls them errors and hidden faults.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card calls hidden faults 'one kind of sin.' Psalm 19:12 calls them 'errors' and 'hidden faults.' Only 19:13 uses the word 'sins,' for willful sins.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answers aren't believable. Nobody would pray for their words to be 'forgotten' or 'hidden' in God's sight, so the baker can spot 'pleasing' without reasoning.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.
